To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain regions involved in creative cognition can be identified by using a novel experimental design that isolates the specific cognitive processes underlying creative thinking.
the neural signature of creative thinking is not as straightforward as previously assumed.
the anterior inferior frontal cortex, the temporal poles, and the lateral frontpolar cortex are selectively involved in conceptual expansion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the human brain is capable of generating novel ideas and concepts, and how it does so.
understanding how the mind works, in particular, how we think and solve problems.
how the brain supports the creative process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural signature of creative cognition is a function of the task and its specific demands.
the neural correlates of creativity depend on the specific type of creativity task used, the type of comparison task used and the specific aspect of creative cognition investigated.
conceptual expansion is associated with a network of regions that are involved in the retention and retrieval of conceptual information and in the control of attentional resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

creativity is a complex cognitive process which requires both the ability to expand and integrate conceptual knowledge as well as to flexibly switch attention between different mental representations.
conceptual expansion, as a specific aspect of creative thinking, is supported by a network of brain regions that are involved in the integration, maintenance, and retrieval of conceptual knowledge.
creativity is not one but many things and that it is the interplay between the different processes involved in creativity that ultimately gives rise to the creative product.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neural signature of creativity is not a single, homogenous pattern, but is instead composed of a number of different neural processes, each of which can be investigated separately and in isolation from the others.
creativity is not a single entity but rather a complex construct which can only be understood by taking into account the various processes involved.
conceptual expansion is a unique and critical facet of creativity that can be investigated using fMRI.
